 Referee who apologised after monumental mistake to officiate Portugal vs Denmark 
 Referee who apologised after monumental mistake to officiate Portugal vs Denmark
 LUSA Rade Obrenovic, the 36-year-old Slovenian referee ANP, ANP / Alamy / Profimedia Slovenian referee Rade Obrenovic, who has been appointed by UEFA to take charge of Saturday's Nations League match between Portugal and Denmark, caught fame for all the wrong reasons last year when he made a very controversial decision in a Europa League match between Feyenoord and Aston Villa.
 In the 35th minute, Feyenoord thought they had scored when Ayase Ueda steered a header home from a corner kick. Referee Rade Obrenovic immediately disallowed the goal, signalling a foul by  Tsuyoshi Watanabe on Aston Villa defender Matty Cash , though replays suggested minimal contact.
 Earlier in the 13th minute, Obrenovic also made a controversial decision when he issued only a yellow card to Feyenoord's Anel Ahmedhodzic for a professional foul on Ollie Watkins as the last man. Even after being sent to the pitch-side monitor by VAR for a potential red card review, Obrenovic decided to stick with his yellow card decision.
 Feyenoord manager Robin van Persie later claimed that Obrenovic approached him during the half-time interval and apologised for ruling out the legitimate goal.
 The Slovenian has previously refereed the Portuguese Under-21 national team in the quarter-finals of Euro 2023 against England . Portugal lost 1-0 in Georgia.
 Obrenovic has also had experience officiating Denmark as he was in charge at Parken Stadium on 15 November 2024, when Denmark lost 1–2 to Spain . It was the first match under Brian Riemer as national team coach, and Obrenovic issued six yellow cards during the game.
 This will be Portugal's first match since Cristiano Ronaldo officially left the national team after 23 years, 234 appearances and 146 goals.
 Having won all four of their opening matches, Portugal top the group with 12 points. Denmark are next on six, while Wales and Norway have three each, with the race for the second qualifying place still open.
 Portugal against Denmark is set to take place in Braga on Saturday at 21.00 CET.
